short_description: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory skin condition characterized by accelerated skin cell turnover resulting in thick, scaly plaques.
common_appearance: well-defined red or pink plaques;silvery-white scales;thickened skin;dry cracked areas
general_course: Chronic condition characterized by recurring flare-ups and periods of remission varying in severity.
general_guidance: Keep skin moisturized, avoid known personal triggers such as stress or skin trauma, and consult a dermatologist for personalized management.
when_to_seek_care: Widespread spreading, severe discomfort or pain, joint swelling or pain, signs of secondary infection, or lack of response to routine skin care.
safety_note: Visual assessment is educational only and cannot replace clinical evaluation or skin biopsy.

short_description: Urticaria (hives) is a common vascular skin reaction marked by transient, intensely itchy raised wheals or welts.
common_appearance: raised red or skin-colored wheals;erythematous borders;blanching center when pressed;variable shapes and sizes
typical_locations: trunk;arms;legs;face;can occur anywhere on the body
general_course: Individual wheals typically resolve within 24 hours while new ones may emerge; acute episodes often subside within days to weeks.
general_guidance: Avoid scratching, wear loose clothing, identify and minimize potential triggers, and seek medical evaluation if episodes recur.
when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency care if hives are accompanied by lip/tongue swelling, difficulty breathing, dizziness, or throat tightness (anaphylaxis warning signs).
safety_note: AI classification provides preliminary visual guidance only and does not determine allergic or systemic causes.

short_description: Molluscum contagiosum is a benign viral skin infection caused by a poxvirus that leads to small, firm, dome-shaped papules with central dimpling.
common_appearance: smooth dome-shaped papules;central umbilication or dimple;pearly or flesh-colored;firm texture
general_course: Often self-limiting over months to years as the body clears the virus, though lesions can spread through direct contact or scratching.
general_guidance: Avoid picking or scratching bumps, practice good hand hygiene, and avoid sharing towels or personal items to minimize spread.
when_to_seek_care: Lesions near the eyes, extensive spreading, signs of bacterial superinfection (redness, warmth, pus), or immunocompromised health status.
safety_note: Visual similarity to other papular lesions requires professional medical confirmation.

short_description: Warts (verrucae) are common benign skin growths caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in the top layer of the skin.
common_symptoms: rough texture;occasional tenderness with pressure;mild discomfort
common_appearance: firm rough-surfaced papules;hyperkeratotic texture;tiny black dots representing clotted capillaries;flesh-colored or grayish
general_course: Benign growths that may persist for months or spontaneously regress with immune clearance; may spread locally with trauma.
general_guidance: Keep area clean and dry, avoid picking or biting warts, and wear protective footwear in shared wet areas such as communal showers.
when_to_seek_care: Painful lesions interfering with walking or daily tasks, rapid multiplication, bleeding, atypical colors/borders, or location on sensitive areas.
safety_note: Image-based guidance cannot differentiate all benign growths from other cutaneous lesions.

short_description: Impetigo is a highly contagious superficial bacterial skin infection commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes.
common_appearance: honey-colored crusts;fragile fluid-filled blisters;red sores that break and weep;erythematous base
general_course: Acute bacterial infection that responds promptly to appropriate clinical management; can spread rapidly if unmanaged.
general_guidance: Maintain strict hand hygiene, wash affected areas gently with soap and water, avoid sharing linens, and seek clinical medical assessment.
when_to_seek_care: Prompt medical evaluation is advised for all suspected cases to confirm bacterial etiology and receive proper clinical guidance.
safety_note: Preliminary classification is educational and cannot replace clinical bacterial assessment.

short_description: Acne vulgaris is a common inflammatory disorder of the pilosebaceous unit involving excess sebum production, follicular hyperkeratinization, and Cutibacterium acnes proliferation.
common_symptoms: comedones;mild to moderate pain;tenderness;localized skin inflammation;oiliness
common_appearance: closed comedones (whiteheads);open comedones (blackheads);inflammatory papules;pustules;occasional deeper nodules
general_course: Chronic or intermittent course commonly influenced by hormonal fluctuations, genetics, and environmental factors.
general_guidance: Use gentle non-comedogenic cleansers, avoid aggressive squeezing or picking which increases scarring risk, and consult a healthcare provider for persistent lesions.
when_to_seek_care: Severe nodular or cystic lesions, persistent scarring, significant emotional distress, or failure to improve with gentle daily skincare.
safety_note: Image evaluation is preliminary and not a personalized clinical treatment plan.

short_description: Vitiligo is an autoimmune condition in which the body's immune system attacks melanocytes, leading to progressive patches of skin depigmentation.
common_symptoms: loss of skin color;occasional mild itching before new patches appear;premature whitening of hair in affected areas
common_appearance: sharply demarcated macules and patches;complete loss of pigment (chalk-white or milky-white);normal skin texture without scaling
general_course: Chronic condition that often progresses unpredictably over time, with periods of stability alternating with pigment loss.
general_guidance: Protect depigmented areas with broad-spectrum sunscreen to prevent sunburn, avoid repetitive skin friction, and consult a dermatologist for educational guidance.
when_to_seek_care: Rapidly expanding depigmented areas, involvement of large body surfaces, or when seeking professional guidance on available medical management strategies.
safety_note: Educational assessment only; Wood's lamp examination or dermatologist evaluation is required for accurate clinical assessment.
